explanation: Retire the established palm-obstructed near-horizontal long-side family, rather than replaying its clear high alignments. Preserve the frame-216 rejection and uncertainty floor. Assess a different contact topology: opposing physical short end walls, closing along the package's long axis with an upright tool. A separately reviewed 30 mm observation rise may expose the occluded end; execute it only when clear and useful, never replay it after acknowledged motion, and otherwise allow stationary measurement. Reacquire the printed landmarks, counter, end strips and broad top-plane support; old pixels are not reused. Independent landmark validation and an axis check prevent relabelling the old long-side contact as an end pinch. Only upright 0, +/-5, +/-10 and +/-20 degree candidates are screened, with existing clearance, overlap and uncertainty requirements unchanged. An infeasible new interval stops approach with recorded operands and requests supported presentation change or genuinely different contact geometry, not another height search. Finger-only screens remain necessary but insufficient: separate full-hand reviews and measured inner-pad aperture authorize descent and closure. Unknown aperture may permit separately clear observation alignment, never contact. Preserve the differential retained-lift verifier and recheck observation reserves before descent and closure.
interface: Apply these 12 exact replacements to previous_method.source. The assembled main(api) implements alternate_pickup only and returns stage_status, reason, evidence, handoff and completion_proposed=false. No new checkpoint names. alt.model stores current end-wall/top/counter receipts, printed-landmark reference validation, end-contact axis validation, preserved guard, upright interval screens and the excluded frame-216 route. Fresh s0..s3 are independently identified plane support, not renamed t0..t3 landmarks. alt.progress records optional observation-rise authorization and actual whole-lease motion. alt.failure records the prevented action, operands, allowances, thresholds and residual margins, including aperture and observation-resource gates. Aperture diagnostics preserve available inner-pad point receipts even when incomplete. alt.effect retains the existing postclosure baseline and measured object-versus-hand lift test, only if reached. Existing secure.* records remain historical. Checkpoint keys may be absent before their phase executes. Coordinates remain world meters, tool-to-world xyzw and top-left image pixels. Repaired execution uses the actual robot state; no automatic reopening, reset, old-pixel replay, transport or placement is added. Handoff identifies checkpoint provenance and assumptions, not future control code.
jev_protocol:
Preserve the seven explicit real-Jev questions. x/y/z/rx/ry/rz read state.processed_features.axes.<axis>.goal_relation: decrease selects negative, within_tolerance selects hold, increase selects positive. Signs denote world translation coordinates or world rotation-vector components. The gripper question reads state.processed_features.objective.gripper and dispatches open, close or keep unchanged. Observation/approach/lift moves request keep; closure remains one bounded episode, never proof of retention. Jev receives processed numerical features and action-specific gate results, not images, hidden geometry or requests to calculate metrics.

All physical actions remain api.drive or api.control. The optional observation rise holds the measured orientation and raises the measured pad center by 0.030 m only after its own full-hand sweep review. Existing drive limits remain at most three leases of at most 16 calls, three native steps per update, 0.008 m translation and 0.08 rad rotation limits, with remaining-budget allocation and phase reserves. Whole-lease api.state comparisons distinguish lease_exhausted with measured progress from stalls or ineffective correction, which stop. Inherited phase names used for budget accounting do not reinstate excluded side-entry orientations. High alignment and lift retain 0.002 m position tolerance; descent retains 0.0005 m and 0.01 rad tolerances incorporated in the geometric allowances. Required counter clearance stays 0.003 m, guarded overlap 0.005 m and nominal overlap at least 0.007 m; the inherited uncertainty guard is not reduced.

Membership, measurement_errors, frame and surface identity are checked before geometric use. The printed landmarks validate affected historical references after observation motion; fresh broad surface points replace stale plane support. Passing a plane or finger-envelope screen grants no action permission. The inner aperture is measured opposing inner-pad separation projected onto the current tool closing axis, not qpos or outer span. Its required width includes two surface guards, two position allowances and two rotational lever allowances. Unknown aperture preserves a separately clear observation alignment but blocks descent/closure; measured insufficient aperture is an established obstruction. A bounded complementary measurement can replace unknown aperture. Full palm/finger sweep review remains independent; hidden clearance is not certified. Four further action/effect reviews plus two supervision reviews are reserved before descent, and postclosure/lift-verification reviews plus supervision are rechecked before closing.

Pose attainment never establishes pickup. Stage completion still requires fresh same-package identity, visible counter separation and retained opposed contact after the differential lift. Independently identified printed landmarks can replace optional quality-checked tracking. geo.attachment_error compares corresponding object points with the actual measured TCP transform. Hand rise must exceed max(0.020 m,6u), object rise max(0.015 m,4u), attachment error must be at most 2u+0.002 m and rotation change at most 0.04 rad. Failed measurements or margins preserve the actual state and produce diagnostic blocked/needs_replan outcomes. completion_proposed always remains false.
